context_chunks.text: Postal NTK timing. Assess the statutory delivery timing applicable to a postal Notice to Keeper before alleging lateness. Do not allege a timing failure until the correct statutory calculation is confirmed. Only after the deterministic timing calculation confirms the failure may the letter state that the NTK was not given within the statutory period for the postal route, so keeper liability is not established under Schedule 4.

Keeper liability threshold. Keeper liability is not automatic. If the operator seeks recovery from the keeper under Schedule 4, the applicable statutory conditions must be satisfied. State that liability cannot be transferred to the keeper under Schedule 4. Do not say the underlying charge is automatically invalid merely because keeper liability fails.

actual.letter:
I write as the registered keeper of vehicle FD18BOF in respect of Parking Charge Notice SP62712518. I dispute liability for this parking charge and require the operator to consider this appeal.

The Parking Charge Notice alleges: 10/08/2026 at B&M Chatham - ME4 4HA.

Where the operator seeks to recover the parking charge from the registered keeper rather than the driver, it must establish that the statutory conditions for keeper liability under Schedule 4 of the Protection of Freedoms Act 2012 have been satisfied. Keeper liability does not arise merely because an individual is the registered keeper.

This appeal is submitted by the registered keeper. No admission is made as to the identity of the driver, and nothing contained within this appeal should be interpreted as identifying or inferring the identity of the driver.

The operator has not established the identity of the driver. As the applicable Schedule 4 requirements have also not been satisfied, liability cannot be transferred to the registered keeper under Schedule 4.

For the verified reasons set out above, the operator has not established keeper liability under Schedule 4 of the Protection of Freedoms Act 2012. The charge should therefore be cancelled as against the registered keeper.

On the operator's own documents the parking event took place on 10 August 2026, the Notice to Keeper was issued on 27 August 2026; the statutory period for delivery of the notice ended on 24 August 2026 and it is deemed delivered on 1 September 2026, 8 days outside that period, so the notice was not delivered within the statutory period and keeper liability does not transfer.

The Notice to Keeper was not delivered within the applicable statutory period for the relevant postal-notice route. The operator has therefore failed to satisfy a condition required to transfer liability to the registered keeper under Schedule 4.

For the reasons set out above, the parking charge is disputed and the operator is requested to cancel the Parking Charge Notice.
